mainTopic: Pesachim 22a: Defending רבי אבהו's rule that 'לא יאכל' forbids benefit, against challenges from גיד הנשה and from blood.
overview: This amud joins the sugya in the middle. The גמרא is testing רבי אבהו's rule: wherever the Torah says 'it may not be eaten,' benefit is forbidden too, unless the Torah makes an exception, as it does for נבילה. First the גמרא finishes explaining how רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר each use the word 'אותו' in the טריפה verse, and why רבי יהודה needs no verse for חולין שנשחטו בעזרה. Then רבי יצחק נפחא challenges the rule from גיד הנשה, which a משנה lets a person send to a non-Jew. The answer is that the נבילה permission covers the whole animal, sinews included. The גמרא shows this works for both views: רבי יהודה holds sinews have flavor and permits benefit, while רבי שמעון holds they have no flavor and forbids benefit. Next comes a challenge from Temple blood sold as fertilizer. The answer is that the Torah compares blood to water ('pour it out like water'), so blood may be used. Finally, רב אשי explains that this means ordinary poured water, not altar or idolatrous libations, which the Torah calls ניסוך.

steps.title: Only the טריפה may be thrown to the dog, not other forbidden foods
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה's derivation is completed. The word 'אותו' teaches that only טריפה may be given to a dog. All other Torah איסורים are forbidden in benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'It' you may throw to the dog, but you may not throw to the dog all the other prohibited items in the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a derivation from the previous discussion. The extra word 'אותו' ('it') in the verse 'לַכֶּלֶב תַּשְׁלִכוּן אֹתוֹ' teaches that only טריפה is permitted for benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reads the נבילה verse exactly as written (gift to a גר, sale to a non-Jew), so he cannot use it to learn a general rule. Instead, he learns the general rule from 'אותו'. This limits the permission to טריפה, so every other Torah איסור stays forbidden in benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It.' The limiting word in the verse about טריפה
Throw to the dog, meaning you get benefit from it
Items forbidden by Torah law
An animal that was fatally injured or torn

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the END of a derivation that began on the previous section of the דף. It is not a brand-new statement. It expresses רבי יהודה's approach.

phrases.english: It, you may throw to the dog,
phrases.notes: 'It' here means the טריפה meat from the פסוק in שמות כב:ל.

phrases.english: but you may not throw to the dog
all the prohibited items in the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the derivation from the previous section of the דף
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי יהודה, 'אותו' limits the benefit permission to טריפה. All other Torah איסורים are forbidden in benefit.

steps.title: What does רבי מאיר learn from 'אותו'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר already learns the general benefit-prohibition elsewhere. So what does he do with the word 'אותו'?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר? (What does he learn from 'it'?)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי מאיר does with the extra word 'אותו'. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר does not need 'אותו' to learn that other איסורים are forbidden in benefit, because he gets that from the נבילה verse. So the word seems extra for him, and the גמרא wants to know what it teaches.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir?
phrases.notes: He's asking: what does רבי מאיר learn from the word 'אותו'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the other opinion uses the same word
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי מאיר learns from the extra word 'אותו'

steps.title: רבי מאיר learns about חולין slaughtered in the עזרה
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר uses 'אותו' to teach that חולין שנשחטו בעזרה may not be given to a dog.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'It' you may throw to the dog, but you may not throw to the dog non-sacred animals slaughtered in the Temple courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי מאיר uses 'אותו' to exclude a specific item: חולין שנשחטו בעזרה, which are forbidden in benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same limiting word teaches each opinion something different. For רבי מאיר, it adds a new benefit-prohibition on non-sacred meat slaughtered in the עזרה. This shows he holds that prohibition is from the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary, non-sacred animals
That were slaughtered
The courtyard of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: It, you may throw to the dog,
but you may not throw to the dog
non-sacred animals slaughtered in the Temple courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹתוֹ אַתָּה מַשְׁלִיךְ לַכֶּלֶב, וְאִי אַתָּה מַשְׁלִיךְ לַכֶּלֶב חוּלִּין שֶׁנִּשְׁחֲטוּ בַּעֲזָרָה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר learns from 'אותו' that חולין שנשחטו בעזרה are forbidden in benefit.

steps.title: Where does רבי יהודה learn about חולין in the עזרה?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה used 'אותו' for the general rule. So where does he learn the law of חולין שנשחטו בעזרה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other (רבי יהודה)? (From where does he learn this?)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to רבי יהודה. He already used 'אותו' for something else, so where is his source for חולין בעזרה? This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word can only be used once. Since רבי יהודה spent 'אותו' on the general rule, he seems to be missing a source for this law.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And the other one?' Asking about the second opinion

phrases.english: And the other?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the same question toward the other opinion
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי יהודה's source for the benefit-prohibition of חולין שנשחטו בעזרה

steps.title: For רבי יהודה, חולין in the עזרה is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה needs no verse, because he holds the prohibition on חולין שנשחטו בעזרה is not from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: Non-sacred animals slaughtered in the courtyard are not forbidden by Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה does not need a verse at all. For him, this prohibition is only דרבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rabbinic prohibition needs no פסוק. So the question about רבי יהודה's source falls away. The two תנאים disagree about whether this law is דאורייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Not from the Torah (only rabbinic)

steps.whatToRemember: The word 'אותו' teaches different things to each opinion. רבי יהודה learns that all Torah איסורים are forbidden in benefit. רבי מאיר learns that חולין שנשחטו בעזרה are forbidden in benefit. For רבי יהודה, that second law is only rabbinic.

phrases.english: Non-sacred animals slaughtered in the courtyard
are not forbidden by Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוּלִּין שֶׁנִּשְׁחֲטוּ בַּעֲזָרָה לָאו דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4 and closes the 'אותו' discussion
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה holds that the prohibition is rabbinic, so he needs no verse.

steps.title: Challenge from גיד הנשה, which may be sent to a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק נפחא objects. The Torah says 'לא יאכלו' about גיד הנשה, yet a משנה lets a person send a thigh with the גיד inside to a non-Jew. That is benefit from it!
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק נפחא objected: But there is the גיד הנשה. The Torah says 'Therefore the children of Israel shall not eat the גיד הנשה,' and we learned in a משנה: A person may send a thigh to a non-Jew with the גיד הנשה inside, because its place is recognizable!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק נפחא attacks רבי אבהו's rule. גיד הנשה is written with 'לא יאכלו', yet benefit from it is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רבי אבהו's rule, 'לא יאכלו' should forbid benefit too. Sending the thigh as a gift is a kind of benefit. The משנה only worries that a Jew might eat it, and it solves that because the גיד's place is visible. It never worries about benefit, so benefit seems to be permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: The sciatic nerve, forbidden to eat (בראשית לב:לג)
'The Merciful One.' The Torah or ה׳
Thigh
Its place is recognizable

steps.confusionAlert: 'מקומו ניכר' is NOT the reason benefit is allowed. It only answers a different worry: that a Jew might think the גיד was removed and eat the thigh. The objection is that the משנה allows the gift at all.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha objected:
But there is the sciatic nerve,
about which the Merciful One said:
'Therefore the children of Israel shall not eat
the sciatic nerve,'
and we learned: A person may send a thigh to a non-Jew,
with the sciatic nerve inside it,
because its place is recognizable!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא: וַהֲרֵי גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge to רבי אבהו's general rule
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's rule that 'לא יאכל' forbids benefit too
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: גיד הנשה is written with 'לא יאכלו', yet the משנה permits benefit (sending it to a non-Jew).

steps.title: גיד הנשה is included in the נבילה permission
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו holds that when the Torah allowed benefit from נבילה, it allowed the whole animal: its meat, its fats, and its sinews.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו holds: When the carcass was permitted, it, its fat, and its sinew were all permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אבהו. The גיד does not break his rule; it is covered by the Torah's explicit exception for נבילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah lets you give or sell a נבילה to a non-Jew. That permission covers the whole carcass, including the גיד. So benefit from גיד הנשה comes from an explicit exception, and the general rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (this view)
An animal that died without proper שחיטה
Was permitted
Its forbidden fats

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu holds:
when the carcass was permitted (for benefit),
it, its fat, and its sinew were permitted.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Places the case under an existing explicit exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: גיד הנשה seemed to show that 'לא יאכלו' does not forbid benefit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The benefit comes from the Torah's נבילה permission, which covers the whole animal, sinews included.

steps.title: The answer only works if sinews have the taste of meat
steps.stepSummary: The answer is fine for the view that sinews give flavor, so they count as meat. But for the view that sinews have no flavor, why should the נבילה permission include them?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says sinews give flavor. But for the one who says sinews do not give flavor, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 7. It only fits one of two opinions about sinews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If sinews give flavor, they count as part of the meat, so the נבילה permission covers them. If sinews are just tasteless 'wood,' they are not part of the נבילה at all. Then the נבילה permission would not reach them, and the original challenge returns.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well (for one view)
Gives flavor
Sinews
What can be said? (signals a challenge)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the defense in step 7 depends on a dispute about sinews. Steps 9–10 answer this by showing that the 'no flavor' view (רבי שמעון) also forbids benefit from the גיד.

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says
'sinews give flavor.'
But according to the one who says
'sinews do not give flavor,'
what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר יֵשׁ בְּגִידִין בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the נבילה permission includes the גיד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If sinews have no flavor, they are not 'meat' of the נבילה, so the נבילה permission should not cover them.

steps.title: The no-flavor view belongs to רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The view that sinews have no flavor is רבי שמעון's. This is shown from a ברייתא about eating the גיד הנשה of a non-kosher animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the one you heard say that sinews do not give flavor? It is רבי שמעון. A ברייתא teaches: someone eats the גיד הנשה of a non-kosher animal. רבי יהודה says he gets two sets of lashes. רבי שמעון says he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering the challenge from step 8. It first identifies who holds that sinews have no flavor: רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה gives two punishments: one for גיד הנשה and one for eating a non-kosher animal. The second punishment means he treats the sinew as real meat with flavor. רבי שמעון exempts the person completely, for two reasons. First, the איסור of גיד הנשה applies only to a kosher animal. Second, the sinew has no meat flavor, so it does not count as non-kosher meat either. The second reason shows that he holds sinews have no flavor.

keyTerms.meaning: Gives flavor; has a real meat taste
Sinews
A non-kosher animal
Makes him liable for two punishments
Exempts

phrases.english: Whom did you hear that said
"sinews do not give flavor"?
It is Rabbi Shimon, as it was taught in a baraita:
One who eats from the sciatic nerve
of a non-kosher animal
Rabbi Yehuda holds him liable for two sets of lashes,
phrases.notes: One for גיד הנשה and one for non-kosher meat.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon exempts him.
phrases.notes: The איסור of גיד הנשה applies only to a kosher animal. The sinew also has no meat flavor, so it does not count as non-kosher meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the challenge in step 8 by identifying who holds the 'no flavor' view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies which תנא holds the problematic view, as setup for showing he is consistent.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Whoever holds that sinews have no flavor would have to allow benefit from גיד הנשה, and that would contradict רבי אבהו.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'no flavor' view is רבי שמעון's. We now need to check what he holds about benefit.

steps.title: רבי שמעון really does forbid benefit from the sinew
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי שמעון forbids benefit from גיד הנשה. So רבי אבהו fits his view too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And indeed, רבי שמעון does forbid benefit. A ברייתא teaches: benefit from גיד הנשה is allowed. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי שמעון forbids it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. It proves that רבי שמעון, who says sinews have no flavor, really does forbid benefit from גיד הנשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, the sinew is not part of the נבילה permission, so 'לא יאכלו' forbids benefit from it, just as רבי אבהו says. For רבי יהודה, the sinew has flavor, so the נבילה permission covers it. That is why benefit is allowed in his view. So רבי אבהו works for both views.

keyTerms.meaning: So too; indeed it is so
Forbids benefit

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אבהו's rule works for both views. רבי יהודה: sinews have flavor, so they are included in the נבילה permission, and benefit is allowed. רבי שמעון: sinews have no flavor, so they are not included, and benefit is forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think this step proves רבי אבהו wrong. The משנה about sending the thigh to a non-Jew simply follows רבי יהודה. רבי שמעון disagrees and forbids benefit, which fits רבי אבהו perfectly.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon, so too indeed,
prohibits deriving benefit, as it was taught in a baraita:
The sciatic nerve is permitted for benefit;
this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda,
and Rabbi Shimon prohibits it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הָכִי נָמֵי דְּאָסַר בַּהֲנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 9 by proving רבי שמעון's position on benefit.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון, who holds sinews have no flavor, forbids benefit from גיד הנשה, so רבי אבהו fits his view.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording a dispute: רבי יהודה permits benefit from גיד הנשה, and רבי שמעון forbids it.

steps.title: Challenge from Temple blood sold as fertilizer
steps.stepSummary: The Torah says not to eat blood, yet the Temple's leftover blood was sold to gardeners. That shows benefit from blood is allowed, which seems to contradict רבי אבהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about blood? The Torah says: 'No soul of you shall eat blood.' Yet a משנה teaches: both kinds of blood mix in the Temple's water channel. They flow out to נחל קדרון and are sold to gardeners as fertilizer. And one who uses it without paying commits מעילה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge to רבי אבהו using blood. Blood may not be eaten, yet people clearly benefited from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אבהו, 'לא תאכל דם' should also forbid benefit from blood. But the משנה describes the Temple selling blood to gardeners. It even says using it without paying is מעילה, misuse of holy property. That treats the blood as something of value you may benefit from.

keyTerms.meaning: But look at; what about (introduces a counter-example)
The water channel that ran through the Temple courtyard
The Kidron Valley, outside Jerusalem
To use as fertilizer
They commit מעילה, misuse of holy property

phrases.english: But there is blood, about which the Merciful One says:
"No soul of you shall eat blood" (Leviticus 17:12),
and we learned in a mishna: Both these and these
phrases.notes: Two kinds of leftover blood from the Temple altar.

phrases.english: mix in the water channel,
and flow out to the Kidron Valley,
and are sold to gardeners as fertilizer,
and one who uses it without paying misuses consecrated property!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the גיד הנשה challenge is resolved, a new counter-example against רבי אבהו is raised.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's rule that 'לא יאכל' also forbids benefit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Blood falls under 'לא תאכל', so by רבי אבהו benefit should be forbidden. Yet the Temple sold blood as fertilizer, and using it is even counted as misuse of something valuable.

steps.title: Blood is compared to water, so benefit is allowed
steps.stepSummary: Blood is an exception. The Torah compares it to water, and just as water may be used, so may blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Blood is different, because the Torah links it to water. It is written: 'You shall not eat it; you shall pour it out on the ground like water.' Just as water is allowed for benefit, so too blood is allowed for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the blood challenge. Blood has its own special Torah source that allows benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו's general rule still stands: 'לא יאכל' normally forbids benefit too. But the verse puts blood next to water ('pour it out like water'). That comparison teaches that blood is permitted for benefit, just like water. So blood is an exception to the rule. It does not disprove the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
It is compared (by a היקש, a link the Torah makes between two things)
Pour it out like water

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אבהו's rule survives. Blood is a special exception because the Torah compares it to water, which may be used for benefit.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא handles counter-examples to a general rule. It finds a specific verse that makes the case an exception, rather than giving up the rule.

phrases.english: Blood is different, as it is compared to water,
as it is written: "You shall not eat it; upon the earth
you shall pour it out like water" (Deuteronomy 12:24).
Just as water is permitted for benefit,
so too blood is permitted for benefit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the blood challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special verse creates an exception to the general rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since blood may not be eaten, רבי אבהו should forbid benefit from it, yet the Temple sold it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Blood is permitted for benefit because the Torah compares it to water. רבי אבהו's general rule remains intact.

steps.title: Maybe blood is like the water poured on the altar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the blood-water comparison. Perhaps blood is like the holy water libation on the מזבח, which is forbidden for benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead: like the water that is poured as a libation on the altar!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 12. Not all water is permitted, so maybe blood is compared to the forbidden kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 assumed that 'like water' means water we may use. But the water poured on the מזבח during סוכות (ניסוך המים) is holy, and benefit from it is forbidden. If blood is compared to that water, the comparison would forbid benefit instead of allowing it.

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead (introduces an alternative reading that challenges the answer)
Poured as a libation (a sacred offering pour)
The altar in the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: The verse under discussion is not repeated in this line. It is the one quoted in step 12: "עַל הָאָרֶץ תִּשְׁפְּכֶנּוּ כַּמָּיִם" (pour it on the ground like water). The whole debate is about which 'water' that verse means.

phrases.english: But say: like the water poured as a libation
phrases.notes: Refers to the water libation on סוכות.

phrases.english: upon the altar!
phrases.notes: That water is holy, so benefit from it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא, כַּמַּיִם הַמִּתְנַסְּכִים עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the water comparison given in Step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that comparing blood to water proves benefit is allowed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Some water (the altar libation) is forbidden for benefit, so the comparison could just as easily point to a prohibition.

steps.title: Like water means like most water
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו answers that 'like water' means the usual kind of water, and most water is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: 'Like water' means like most water.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו defends the comparison. He says the verse means ordinary water, the way most water is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most water in the world is not holy, and people may use it. So a plain comparison to 'water' should follow the common case, not the rare holy altar water.

keyTerms.meaning: Most water (the typical, common kind)

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
'Like water' means like most water.
phrases.notes: Most water may be used freely.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ כַּמַּיִם רוֹב מַיִם
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the verse by its common, majority case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Blood could be compared to the forbidden altar water.
steps.terutzMaskana: Blood is compared to ordinary water, which is permitted.

steps.title: The verse does not say most water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבי אבהו's answer, because the verse only says 'like water', not 'like most water'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי אבהו. The word 'most' is not in the verse, so his reading has no basis in the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain 'like water' could include every kind of water, even holy water. Adding 'most' is a guess that the text does not support, so the challenge from Step 13 stands until רב אשי answers it in Step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it written...? (a rhetorical rejection: the text does not say that)

phrases.english: Is 'most water' written?!
phrases.notes: Of course not! The פסוק only says 'like water'.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי אבהו's 'most water' reading entirely
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word 'most' is not in the verse.

steps.title: Water that is poured out, not water offered as a libation
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a new answer. The verse uses the word 'pour' (שפיכה), which means ordinary poured water, not libation water (ניסוך).
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: like water that is poured out, and not like water that is offered as a libation.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי replaces the rejected answer with a better one taken from the verse's own wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says "תִּשְׁפְּכֶנּוּ כַּמָּיִם", pour it like water. Water on the מזבח is never described as 'poured' (שפיכה). It is called a libation (ניסוך). So the verse compares blood to everyday poured-out water, which may be used.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the previous answer and brings a new one)
Poured out (ordinary pouring, the word the verse uses)
Offered as a libation (sacred pouring)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the גמרא reading a single word (תשפכנו) precisely to tell apart two kinds of 'water'.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
like water that is poured out,
phrases.notes: This matches the word in the פסוק: תשפכנו.

phrases.english: and not like water offered as a libation.
phrases.notes: Altar water is called ניסוך, not שפיכה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי כַּמַּיִם הַנִּשְׁפָּכִין וְלֹא כַּמַּיִם הַנִּיסָּכִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer to Step 13 after Step 15 rejected the first answer
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the verse's verb
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Like water' could mean holy libation water.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'pour' points to ordinary water, so benefit from blood is allowed.

steps.title: Maybe blood is like water poured for idolatry
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the verse could mean water poured out before עבודה זרה, which is forbidden for benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: like water that is poured out before idolatry!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests רב אשי's answer. There is another kind of 'poured' water that is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water poured as worship to an idol is forbidden for benefit. If that counts as 'poured' water, then comparing blood to poured water might still mean blood is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Idolatry. Anything offered to it is forbidden for benefit.
Before (in front of)

phrases.english: But say: like water that is poured out
before idolatry!
phrases.notes: Such water is forbidden for benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא כַּמַּיִם הַנִּשְׁפָּכִין לִפְנֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's answer in Step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that 'poured water' means only permitted water
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Water poured for idolatry is also 'poured' and is forbidden, so the comparison could still lead to a prohibition.

steps.title: Idolatrous pouring is also called a libation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that pouring for עבודה זרה is also called ניסוך, as the verse says 'drink the wine of their libations'. So it is not the 'poured' water of our verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too it is called a libation, as it is written: 'they drank the wine of their libations'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אשי. The Torah calls idolatrous pouring ניסוך too, so it falls outside the word 'poured' just like altar water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in דברים לב:לח uses נסיכם (their libations) for idol offerings. Both the holy pourings and the idolatrous ones are therefore 'libations' (ניסוך). Only ordinary water is plain 'poured', so blood is compared to ordinary water, and benefit from blood is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: There (in that case)
Libation, a ritual pouring offered as worship
It is called
The wine of their libations (from דברים לב:לח)

steps.whatToRemember: Blood is compared to water that is 'poured' (שפיכה), meaning ordinary water. Holy altar pourings and idolatrous pourings are both called ניסוך, so neither is meant. That is why benefit from blood is permitted, the exception to רבי אבהו's rule.

phrases.english: There too it is called a libation,
phrases.notes: Idolatrous pouring counts as ניסוך, not plain שפיכה.

phrases.english: as it is written: 'they drank the wine of their libations.'
